record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Find an explicit computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the square lattice and, for a finite region $\Lambda$, a translation-invariant tensor network state (projected entangled pair state, PEPS) constructed from a single five-index tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4}$, where $d$ is the physical dimension and $D$ is the bond dimension. For a rectangular block $R$ of sites, contracting the bond indices internally while leaving the physical indices and the boundary virtual indices open defines a linear map
$$A_R: (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes \partial R} \longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes R},$$
sending a configuration of boundary virtual states to the corresponding physical vector.

Definitions. The tensor $A$ is called injective on a region $R$ if the map $A_R$ is injective. The tensor $A$ is called normal if there exists some finite rectangular block on which $A_R$ becomes injective. For a normal tensor $A$, the injectivity index $I(A)$ is defined as the smallest positive integer $L$ such that $A_R$ is injective for every rectangular block $R$ of side lengths at least $L$.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit, computable function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ — preferably polynomial in $D$ — such that for every normal PEPS tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$ (and arbitrary physical dimension $d$) one has
$$I(A) \le f(D).$$
Equivalently, give a concrete computable upper bound on the size of the blocking region needed to certify injectivity, depending only on the bond dimension $D$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on PEPS continues to list the determination of an explicit (ideally polynomial) computable bound on the injectivity index of normal PEPS in terms of the bond dimension as an open problem. Known partial results exist (e.g., bounds of order roughly D^2 log D in related MPS/PEPS contexts), but no proven optimal or fully satisfactory polynomial bound in the PEPS setting has been established as of recent surveys and follow-up work.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Lists explicit open questions including a computable bound on the injectivity index of normal PEPS in terms of bond dimension.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of an explicit computable (polynomial) bound on the PEPS injectivity index is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on injective PEPS still treats the injectivity blocking length as a parameter rather than providing an explicit polynomial bound in D.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature does not provide an explicit polynomial bound, consistent with the problem remaining open.

status_evidence.title: A generalization of the injectivity condition for Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes injectivity conditions for PEPS but does not resolve the question of an explicit computable upper bound on the injectivity index.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit computable bound on the injectivity index has been provided in subsequent generalizations.
